**Not ready to publish.** Two claims break the brand policy.

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website" | Allowlisted, exact wording (review export, Oct 2026) |
| "The finest organic loose leaf" | **"finest" is an unprovable superlative (section 3).** "Organic" is backed, but only as "Certified organic by the Soil Association" |
| "eco-friendly bags" | **General environmental claim, banned (section 3).** The backed claim is "plastic-free and home compostable" |
| "packed by hand in Bristol" | Allowlisted, but the wording covers "every tin". Check that the bags are also packed by hand, or keep the claim to the tins |

**Other checks**
- No banned voice words, no exclamation marks, no fake urgency, no invented numbers.
- Under the claims-guard rule, the landing page must make any claim that ads make. This is the landing page, so the claims here are the source.
- Per section 6, Sam needs to approve it before it goes live.

**Suggested rewrite**

> Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website. Certified organic by the Soil Association loose leaf tea, and plastic-free, home compostable tea bags. Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol.

```json
{"issues": [{"quote": "The finest organic loose leaf", "type": "superlative"}, {"quote": "eco-friendly bags", "type": "green_claim"}], "publish": false}
```
